items.text: StoreError has a variant LeafDurabilityUncertain carrying the leaf index and the failed flush's std::io::Error as its source, its message naming both, distinct from Io and from LeafAlreadyWritten, and LeafStore::put_leaf's documented errors name it.

FileLeafStore::put_leaf writes and flushes a leaf's bytes in a dot-prefixed temporary file in leaves/, named by leaf_temp_name from the process id, the index and a sequence the caller supplies (a process-wide counter for put_leaf) and created with create_new so it never replaces an existing file, before any file exists under the leaf's 20-digit name, and removes that temporary file when writing or flushing it fails.

put_leaf gives the leaf its final name with a link that refuses to replace an existing entry, and an existing final name returns LeafAlreadyWritten for that index with the existing bytes unchanged and this writer's temporary file removed.
A successful link advances the extent; put_leaf then removes the temporary name and flushes leaves/, and a failure to remove the temporary name still returns Ok.
A failure to flush leaves/ after the link returns LeafDurabilityUncertain for that index, and the handle refuses every further put_leaf with that error until the store is reopened.
FileLeafStore::open flushes leaves/ before it counts the leaves, and when that flush fails it returns Io naming the leaves directory and the flush, and writes nothing.
FileLeafStore::open never counts, deletes or changes a leftover dot-prefixed temporary file in leaves/.
FileLeafStore::open_read_only performs FileLeafStore::open's checks without flushing leaves/, counts the named leaves, and does not fail because a flush of leaves/ would fail.
put_leaf on a handle from FileLeafStore::open_read_only returns StoreError::ReadOnly naming the store's directory and the act, and writes nothing.
pin on a handle from FileLeafStore::open_read_only returns StoreError::ReadOnly naming the store's directory and the act, and leaves state.json and the pinned root unchanged.
file.rs's module docs state that a named leaf is whole and flushed, that only hidden temporary files may be partial, and that the link is the commit point.
A fault seam that fails a chosen step of put_leaf or the leaves/ flush at open exists in FileLeafStore and compiles only under cfg(test).
file_tests.rs holds the eighteen new tests of LYSLOGSTORE-001 R8, names the no-replace link wherever it named create_new, and each drift injection in its module-doc tables fails exactly its own test.
Every leg of the design's gate array passes and file.rs stays under 500 lines of code.
DIRECTORY-003's depends_on names LYSLOGSTORE-001 after DIRECTORY-002, and no other field of DIRECTORY-003 changes.
Anchor::open_read_only's doc examples and lys-anchor's read-only tests open their store with FileLeafStore::open_read_only.
Log::open_at_pin opens a store found one leaf ahead of its pin at the pinned head without pinning, reports the pending repair, and refuses to append while it is pending; Log::open alone repairs.

Anchor::open_read_only never repairs a store found one leaf ahead of its pin: it opens at the pinned head, and its status says in words that one leaf stands ahead of the pin and that a writable open repairs it.
